The FP32 intermediate error (~1e-7) exceeds the ~5e-10 distance-to-tie, flipping the final rounding. This is a genuine in-scope contract violation. I'll finalize the evidence and verdict.

message.reasoning_content:
7 mismatches, off by one ulp. But wait — could my reference itself be wrong? The kernel error for x=0.0029296875: exact sigmoid ≈ 0.500732...? sigmoid(0.00293) ≈ 0.50 + 0.0014646/... let's compute: sigmoid(x)=0.5+x/4 approx = 0.5+0.0007324=0.5007324. FP16 values near: 0.50048828125 (0x3801... actually 0x3801=0.50048828125? 0x3800=0.5, 0x3801=0.50048828125 yes). 0.5007324 is exactly halfway between 0.50048828 and 0.50097656! Tie → round to even: 0x3801 (odd) vs 0x3802 (even). 0.5007324 is midpoint; even is 0x3802 (0.50097656). Wait the midpoint of 0.50048828125 and 0.5009765625 is 0.500732421875. sigmoid(0.0029296875) = 0.5 + tanh(x/2)/2 = 0.5 + x/4 - x³/48... = 0.5+0.00073242187 - tiny = slightly less than midpoint → rounds to 0x3801 = 0.50048828. Kernel gave 0x3802. So kernel is off — FP32 rounding error flipped a near-tie. These are exact-boundary cases. So confirmed: kernel mismatches on legal inputs.

But need to double check reference computation is exact — FP64 sigmoid with a single rounding should be reliable; mismatch is 1 ulp on near-tie cases, and true value is below midpoint. Let me verify one case precisely with high precision to be safe. Quick check: sigmoid(0.0029296875). Using math: exp(x) ≈ 1+x+x²/2+x³/6. sigmoid = (1+tanh(x/2))/2. x/2=0.00146484375. tanh(y)=y - y³/3 = 0.00146484375 - 1.05e-9 = 0.0014648427. /2 = 0.00073242135. sigmoid = 0.50073242135. Midpoint = 0.500732421875. True value is 5.25e-10 BELOW the midpoint → correctly rounds to 0.50048828125 (0x3801). Kernel gives 0.5009765625 (0x3802). Confirmed defect.

The FP32 computation: value in FP32 also can't represent exactly; error ~1e-7 > 5e-10 gap. Confirmed.

Finalize evidence, update claim, verdict reject.
